title: Probe and needle on the patient
view: Prone right leg seen from above and the lateral side (after NYSORA's patient view, pulled back): thigh on the left, knee and calf on the right; the broad upper surface is the back of the leg, the lower band the lateral thigh.
teachingPoint: Find the popliteal crease and the biceps femoris tendon, scan up about 6 cm to where the nerves join, and go in-plane from the lateral thigh just below the probe.
claims: Prone right leg, posterolateral view after NYSORA's patient photo (concept only; owner, 2026-10-02), widened to show the back of the knee.
Dashed: the popliteal crease and the biceps femoris tendon (standard anatomy; the lateral border of the fossa).
Bracket: the probe about 6 cm above the crease, where the nerves join (record).
Needle entering the lateral thigh directly below the probe, in line with it: in-plane from lateral (record).
Labels: Popliteal crease, Biceps femoris tendon, 6 cm, Linear probe, Block needle.

geometry.why: probe proximal to the crease (thigh is left)
probe on the back of the thigh
biceps tendon on the lateral (lower) edge
